summary: Choctaw County lookout completed in 1949 as a 120-foot Aermotor MC-39; the NHLR says it is still used on very high fire danger days.

staffing.status: no staffing details given; NHLR says the tower is still used on very high fire danger days

events.note: NHLR says the tower was completed in 1949; height 120 ft converted to metres

evidence.supports: Built 1949 as a 120-foot Aermotor MC-39; still used on very high fire danger days
evidence.quote: A tall, 120' Aermotor MC-39 model, Scott Mountain Lookout Tower was completed in 1949. It is still used on very high fire danger days.

evidence.supports: Administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
Forest Lookouts page is headed Choctaw County and Alabama Forestry Commission
Forest Lookouts page names the Alabama Forestry Commission

evidence.quote: The most common steel lookout tower model in Alabama's forests was the Aermotor MC-39

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: The NHLR entry is the only substantive source; the Forest Lookouts page carries only a heading. Searches found no other account of this tower's history, staffing or access, so the access and visit keys are omitted. The brief's year (1949), registration date (January 10, 2010), coordinates and elevation check out. The 1819 News article is general Alabama context, not about this tower; the story sentence says so and names the MC-39 itself.
